title: Cash Flow Forecasting
description: Build a defensible cash flow forecast for a small business. Tests financial modelling, assumption quality, and financial storytelling.

seo.overviewTitle: 13-Week Direct Cash Flow Forecasting & Working Capital Management
seo.overviewBody: Cash flow management is the lifeline of corporate and SME operations. Financial analysts demonstrate value by building 13-week direct cash flow models, optimizing working capital timing (Accounts Receivable DSO vs Accounts Payable DPO), and evaluating cash runway under revenue sensitivity scenarios.

deliverables.title: 1. 13-Week Direct Cash Flow Forecast Model
deliverables.desc: Dynamic Excel forecast model (.xlsx) projecting weekly cash inflows, payroll, vendor disbursements, and net cash balances.

deliverables.title: 2. Working Capital & Liquidity Audit Memo
deliverables.desc: Executive memo analyzing Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), inventory holding periods, and vendor payment term negotiations.

deliverables.title: 3. Cash Runway & Sensitivity Scenario Report
deliverables.desc: Sensitivity analysis detailing cash runway durations under best-case, base-case, and downside revenue contraction scenarios.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Direct and Indirect cash flow forecasting?
faqs.answer: Direct cash flow forecasting tracks actual cash receipts from customers and cash payments to suppliers weekly. Indirect forecasting starts with net income and adjusts for non-cash expenses and working capital changes.

faqs.question: How do you calculate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO)?
faqs.answer: DSO = (Accounts Receivable / Total Credit Sales) * Number of Days. Lower DSO indicates faster cash collection from customers.

faqs.question: How do you manage cash flow timing mismatches in South African SMEs?
faqs.answer: Implement strict 30-day credit terms, offer early settlement discounts, request upfront customer deposits, and negotiate aligned payment terms with key suppliers.
